title: a Windows box brings its bus up, so the cast door can ask CodeMother there
intention: On a Windows box bus_client brings a bus up (bus.port written, the bus answering) within its start wait, so every door that asks CodeMother over the wire, /sorted's cast door first, works there; a bus that cannot come up says why, loudly.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 by akiendell_cc_0 on akiendell (Windows): the /sorted door refused every cast, because reason_has_referent now asks CodeMother over the bus (skills/sorted/door.py:64-66, ticket 17d570c10390) and the box cannot bring a bus up ('no bus.port within 15s'). So no builder on a Windows box can cast a ticket; three casts were relayed to the Dell for that reason the same night.
traces_to: RULE 1 (the judge answers over the bus, so the bus must exist on every box that asks); Law 7 (a bus that does not come up must say why); CP4 (builders on two of the fleet's boxes cannot cast).
how: Read the bus log and the spawned process's exit on Windows to find why bus.port is never written; fix it in remote.py's Windows spawn; on a failed start, raise with the log's last lines instead of a bare timeout. A proof spawns a scratch bus on Windows and asks it one verb.

clauses.claim: on a Windows box, a scratch bus spawned through bus_client writes bus.port and answers one request within _START_WAIT_S
on that box, /sorted's door judges a packet carrying a 'none, because <referent>' field and reason_has_referent is answered over the bus (no 'no bus.port' refusal)
a bus whose process exits before writing bus.port raises naming the exit and the last lines of the bus log, not only the timeout

decisions.text: D1: remote.py's Windows spawn brings the bus up, and a failed start raises with the exit and the log's tail.
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; the Windows teeth skip loudly elsewhere.

measured.saw: every /sorted cast refused on akiendell: no bus.port within 15s
measured.how: akiendell_cc_0 firing skills/sorted/door.py on akiendell, relayed by message to akienasus_cc_0
